criteria.name: Problem 6
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 6 (6 pts). Statement: 6. Let M be a map with n≥ 3 hideouts. Prove that 2 ≤ W (M)≤ n, and that these bounds cannot be improved. In other words, prove that for each n≥ 3, there exist maps M1 and M2 such that W (M1) = 2 and W (M2) =n.

criteria.name: Problem 7a
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 7a (3 pts). Statement: 7a. Prove that if M is bipartite, then C(M)≤n/2.

criteria.name: Problem 7b
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 7b (3 pts). Statement: 7b. Prove that C(M)≤n/2 for any map M with the property that, for all hideouts H1 and H2, either all paths from H1 to H2 contain an odd number of edges, or all paths from H1 to H2 contain an even number of edges.

criteria.name: Problem 8
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 8 (4 pts). Statement: 8. A map M is called k-perfect if its hideout set H can be partitioned into equal-sized subsets A1,A2,..., Ak such that for anyj, the hideouts ofAj are only adjacent to hideouts inAj+1 or Aj−1. (The indices are taken modulo k: the hideouts of A1 may be adjacent to the hideouts ofAk.) Show that if M is k-perfect, then C(M)≤ 2n k .

criteria.name: Problem 9
